messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING oncall — SLO breach detected for redwood-prod/shared-gpu-pool (p99 latency > 2.5s for 5m). Pager duty: @alex. CPU/GPU utilization spike + streaming stalls. link: https://console.redwood/alerts/1859876543

alex: ack — looks like a multi-tenant tail issue, getting context now. Starting timeline + impact.

maria: I’m seeing increased IO wait on nvme for nodes gpool-12..gpool-15 in cluster west-us-2, lots of `docker` cgroup throttles. Could be noisy-tenant.

alex: copying logs to thread. runbook step1: identify top tenants by active sessions.

alex: `kubectl top pods -n inference --selector=pool=shared-gpu | sort -k3 -nr | head -n 10` -> heavy hitters: tenant-b, tenant-d, tenant-x. tenant-d has huge streaming sessions.

sre-jordan: observed cgroup blkio throttling counters incrementing on gpool-13. Suspect a tenant doing large model downloads + concurrent streaming -> IO saturation.

eng-paul: possible regression — last deploy to shared-gpu-pool rolled in new caching layer for KV, could cause extra disk hits. Rolling back that deploy to a subset?

alex: mitigation plan (live): 1) throttle evict top noisy tenant sessions, 2) shift some traffic to fallback dedicated model variant in hosted region, 3) spin up a temporary burst node set (if available).

maria: +1 for evicting noisy sessions. I can push rate-limit rules at the router: `redwood-routerctl apply-rate-limit --tenant tenant-d --qps 4` to throttle back.

cs-elaine: heads-up: tenant-d is an active paying customer on Dedicated negotiation. Need to minimize surfaced downtime. If we evict sessions, CS will prepare comms.

alex: understood. Try soft-throttle first (429 with retry-after) not hard draining.

incident-bot: action taken: rate-limit applied by maria at 1859876830, ruleID rl-6e2a.

maria: applied soft throttle, monitored. p95 dropped from 1.2s -> 0.9s in 30s, p99 still around 2.3s. Streaming stalls reduced but tail still high.

sre-jordan: started migrating a few long-lived streaming sessions off gpool-13 to gpool-21 (less loaded). Doing live session migration: `inference-migrate --session-id <id> --dest=gpool-21` (some sessions succeed, some reconnects).

eng-paul: I’m reverting the KV caching change on a canary subset (nodes gpool-12/13) to see IO delta. Revert triggered at 1859877005.

alex: monitoring metrics: NVMe write latency dropped ~35% on gpool-13 after canary revert. p99 trending down. Good signal.

sre-jordan: still seeing occasional GPU stall stack traces pointing to blocking disk reads in uploader threads. Will reduce uploader concurrency on host via cgroup change: `echo 8 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/blkio.throttle.read_bps_device` (applied).

maria: router qps + cgroup throttle + canary revert combined lowered p99 to ~1.5s at 1859877120. Still above objective (1.0s).

alex: next step: enable fallback routing for latency-sensitive routes to `redwood-light` model (smaller model variant) for 5% of traffic from the affected customer-tokens. Configure canary: `routingctl set-fallback --route /v1/stream --matcher tenant_id=tenant-d --percent=5`.

cs-elaine: initiating customer notification template. Will mark impact as "degraded performance, elevated latency" and say mitigation in progress.

incident-bot: fallback rule applied at 1859877230, ruleID fb-9c1.

maria: after fallback + revert + throttles, p99 = 0.95s at 1859877300. Streaming stall errors dropped to baseline.

alex: good. Summarize timeline for postmortem: root cause = noisy neighbor tenant-d causing NVMe IO saturation; contributing factor = recent KV caching change increasing disk hits under load; live mitigations = soft rate-limit, cgroup blkio throttle, session migration, canary revert of KV change, routing fallback.

eng-paul: will open a PR to improve KV cache warmup + add in-memory fallback for cold misses to avoid disk storms (link: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/5231).

sre-jordan: ops follow-ups: 1) add blkio monitor alarm before SLO breach, 2) create automated tenant isolation playbook, 3) add per-tenant streaming session caps in router.

alex: handing off to oncall-next for the overnight watch. @oncall-next please ack and keep this on your shift rotation; check for recurrence for 12h.

oncall-next: acked — will monitor dashboards and keep CS updated if we see p99 creep.

cs-elaine: tagging customers impacted list: tenant-d (high), tenant-x (some), tenant-b (minor). Preparing follow-up notes and rough ETA for formal postmortem.

maria: logging final artifact links: perf dashboard https://console.redwood/metrics/1859876543, node logs s3://redwood-incident-logs/1859876543/, revert PR https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/5232

alex: incident status -> resolved (mitigated) at 1859877400. Will file postmortem, CC infra and product teams. Thanks all. :tada:

incident-bot: incident closed by alex at 1859877600 (severity: SLO-breach, impact: degraded latency for ~18m)."
